claims.text: Elevated configurational entropy stabilizes local atomic-scale disorder in the alloy.
Local atomic-scale disorder enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling enables superconductivity at low temperatures.
The starting material is a near-equiatomic alloy containing several elements.
The superconducting state of the starting material is uncharacterized.
Mixing four or five elements in near-equal proportions produces a high-configurational-entropy variant.
Using fewer elements or a more ordered, non-equiatomic composition produces a reduced-entropy baseline.
High configurational mixing creates local strain fields.
Configurational entropy induces structural heterogeneity that locally breaks lattice symmetry.
Entropy-induced structural heterogeneity modifies the electronic density of states.
The modified electronic structure enhances electron-phonon interactions.
Enhanced electron-phonon interactions facilitate Cooper-pair formation.
The maximally mixed variant will exhibit a distinct superconducting transition.
The maximally mixed variant will have a higher critical current density than the reduced-entropy baseline.
The reduced-entropy baseline will show either no superconductivity or substantially lower superconducting performance.
The proposed mechanism is limited to low temperatures below the critical temperature and alloys with similar elemental constituents.
The beneficial effect is limited to composition ranges where disorder is enhanced without detrimental phase separation.
Impurity phases or alternative pairing channels may contribute to the observed superconductivity.

contradictions.description: The prediction frames the high-entropy variant as having improved superconducting behavior relative to a poorer baseline, but the falsification rule says failure to display a lower onset Tc would refute the hypothesis. A lower Tc would ordinarily be worse, while an equal or higher Tc could be consistent with enhancement, so the direction of the Tc criterion is internally inconsistent.
